Research Proposal: Adapting PCIe Fabric Technology
for Neighborhood-Scale Decentralized Data Networks
Benjamin Niccum
University of Texas at Arlington
December 2025
1 Executive Summary
This research proposal outlines a semester-long investigation into adapting Dolphin’s PCIe fabric
technologies for consumer-scale neighborhood data networks. The project aims to demonstrate
how Device Lending, Reflective Memory, SuperSockets, and SISCI technologies can enable high-
performance, privacy-preserving home data networks that rival cloud storage performance while
maintaining user data sovereignty.
The research represents a significant market opportunity in the rapidly growing consumer pri-
vacy and edge computing sectors, potentially opening new applications for Dolphin’s proven PCIe
fabric technology stack.
2 Research Objectives
2.1 Primary Objective
Demonstrate the feasibility of adapting PCIe fabric technology to create neighborhood-scale decen-
tralized data networks that achieve superior performance compared to traditional home networking
while maintaining strong privacy guarantees.
2.2 Secondary Objectives
• Develop consumer-scale adaptations of Dolphin’s core technologies (Device Lending, Reflec-
tive Memory, SuperSockets, SISCI)
• Quantify energy efficiency improvements of distributed vs. centralized data storage
• Design privacy-preserving protocols for neighborhood-scale resource sharing
• Identify specific commercialization opportunities and market applications
3 Technology Integration Analysis
3.1 Core Technology Synergies
Device Lending → Dynamic Resource Allocation
• Enable sharing of storage devices, GPUs, and compute resources across neighborhood homes
1
Dolphin Research Proposal B. Niccum
• Transparent device access without requiring driver modifications
• Dynamic allocation based on demand patterns and device availability
Reflective Memory → Distributed Consensus
• Ultra-fast (<130ns) data synchronization across neighborhood nodes
• Hardware-accelerated consensus mechanisms for real-time coordination
• Multicast data distribution for neighborhood-wide system updates
SuperSockets → Privacy-Preserving Communication
• 10x performance improvement for home-to-home communication
• Transparent acceleration with integrated privacy protection layers
• Automatic failover between PCIe fabric and internet routing
SISCI API → Neighborhood API (NAPI)
• Consumer-scale version of shared memory interface
• Resource management optimized for home data box environments
• Cross-platform support for heterogeneous consumer hardware
4 Research Methodology
4.1 Semester Research Phase (4 months)
Hardware Configuration
• Dolphin MXE52010 eBox expansion system with MXB585 active backplane
• Option A - PCIe 5.0: MXH532/572 transparent adapters with eXpressWare software suite
• Option B - Gen4 NTB: MXS924 switch, MXH930/914/916/918 NTB adapters with eX-
pressWare licenses
• Standard networking equipment for controlled testing environment
• Power measurement tools for comprehensive energy analysis
Software Development
• Custom Neighborhood API (NAPI) implementation inspired by SISCI concepts
• Privacy-preserving communication protocol development
• Energy monitoring and analysis framework
• GPU sharing simulation inspired by Intel SR-IOV ARC demonstration at SC25
• Integration with current eXpressWare software suite and PCIe 5.0/Gen4 hardware capabilities
2
Dolphin Research Proposal B. Niccum
Experimental Evaluation
• Latency measurements: Target <50ms for neighborhood operations
• Throughput analysis: Demonstrate measurable improvement over standard home networking
• Energy consumption: Quantify efficiency gains vs. cloud storage alternatives
• Privacy validation: Formal analysis of privacy-preserving protocols
4.2 Simulation and Scalability Analysis
Network Simulation Environment
• Discrete-event simulation of 10-50 node neighborhood networks
• Realistic modeling of residential network constraints and characteristics
• Fault injection testing for reliability analysis
• Performance scaling analysis as network size increases
5 Expected Outcomes
5.1 Technical Deliverables
• Working prototype using Dolphin MXE52010 PCIe 5.0 system demonstrating neighborhood
networking concepts
• Performance analysis comparing neighborhood networks vs. cloud alternatives
• Energy consumption model with empirical validation using MXE52010 platform with modular
850W power supply
• Privacy framework design with formal security analysis
• GPU sharing demonstration inspired by SC25 Intel SR-IOV ARC showcase, adapted for
neighborhood scale
5.2 Commercial Value
• Market opportunity identification for Dolphin technology in consumer/SMB sectors
• Technology adaptation roadmap for consumer-scale deployment
• Performance validation data for enterprise technology in new contexts
• Competitive analysis and positioning recommendations
5.3 Academic Contributions
• Novel application of PCIe interconnect technology to consumer networks
• Comprehensive energy analysis of distributed vs. centralized data storage
• Privacy-preserving protocols optimized for neighborhood-scale deployment
• Foundation for continued research in residential high-performance computing

9 Conclusion
This research represents a unique opportunity to extend Dolphin’s proven PCIe fabric technology
into new market segments while addressing growing consumer demands for data privacy and energy
efficiency. The project’s scope is carefully designed to provide meaningful results within a semester
timeframe while establishing a foundation for continued collaboration and commercial development.
The integration of academic rigor with industry partnership ensures that research outcomes
will provide value to both the scientific community and Dolphin’s strategic technology development
initiatives.
